concepts.def: A tiny nucleus of protons and neutrons with electrons in shells.
Types of nuclear radiation with different penetration and ionising power.
Time for half the undecayed nuclei to decay.
Splitting a large nucleus, releasing energy.
Joining small nuclei, releasing energy (powers stars).
Quarks and leptons; protons and neutrons are made of quarks.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nuclear Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nuclear Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Redshift of distant galaxies is evidence that:
options: the universe is contracting
galaxies are heating up
the universe is expanding
light slows over distance

mcqs.q: The Sun is currently in which stage?
options: Protostar
Main sequence
Red giant
White dwarf

mcqs.q: What is the difference between nuclear fission and fusion?
options: Fission splits a heavy nucleus into smaller ones; fusion joins light nuclei into a heavier one.
Fission and fusion are the same process, just at different scales.
Fission combines small atoms into bigger ones, and fusion splits them.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.

mcqs.q: In a balanced nuclear equation, what must be equal on both sides?
options: Only the atomic number (proton count) needs to balance.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
The total mass number (top numbers) and the total atomic number (bottom numbers) must both balance.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Only the total mass in kilograms needs to balance.
Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Main sequence star”?
options: Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).
A stable star (like the Sun) where outward gas pressure balances gravitational collapse.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Redshift”?
options: The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.
Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cosmic microwave background”?
options: Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.
Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).
The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Supernova”?
options: Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.
Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Life cycle of stars”?
options: Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).

options: Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).

Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
